ours-quant.short: Night School's quantisation runs, computed for this film
ours-quant.citation: media/school/quant/facts.json, written by tools/school/fill_quant.mjs from system/school/quant.mjs and quant-gptq.mjs: the attention model's weights quantised by round-to-nearest and GPTQ at 8, 6, 4, 3 and 2 bits, per tensor, per output channel and per group, scored on 1,024 held-out rows with bootstrap intervals; one tensor at a time; controls.
claims: Float loss 0.6676; per channel round-to-nearest 8/6/4/3/2 bits: 0.668, 0.668, 0.675, 0.725, 3.483.
4 bits per channel: 15,376 bytes (18 percent); rise +0.0078 (round-to-nearest) and +0.0028 (GPTQ).
ours-quant.interval: Row bootstrap, paired differences, in facts.json.
ours-quant.does_not_prove: Anything about large models; activations stay in float.

jacob2018.short: Jacob and others 2018, Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only Inference
jacob2018.citation: Jacob, B., Kligys, S., Chen, B., and others (2018). CVPR 2018. arXiv:1712.05877.
claims: Real values are represented by an integer and a scale (and zero point): r = S (q - Z).

dettmers2022.citation: Dettmers, T., Lewis, M., Belkada, Y., Zettlemoyer, L. (2022). LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale. NeurIPS 2022. arXiv:2208.07339.
claims: Large-magnitude outlier features in activations emerge in large transformers and break naive 8-bit quantisation.

frantar2023.citation: Frantar, E., Ashkboos, S., Hoefler, T., Alistarh, D. (2023). GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers. ICLR 2023. arXiv:2210.17323.
claims: Quantises weights column by column, updating the not-yet-quantised weights to compensate, using second-order information from calibration data.
